Acceptance: Client-set role headers are ignored. Add a test asserting injected role headers do not grant privilege.

checks.question: Is the application missing dependency-graph monitoring for transitive vulnerabilities (only top-level deps are scanned)? (V15.1.2)

onYes.title: Fix V15.1.2: scan the full transitive dependency tree
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Critical CVEs often hide in transitive dependencies that surface-level scans miss.

Find all instances: Inspect the SCA configuration; verify it walks the lockfile, not just package.json/requirements.txt.

Fix correctly: Switch to an SCA tool that operates on the lockfile (npm audit, pip-audit, cargo-audit, grype). Wire it into CI to block on critical/high findings.

Acceptance: SCA covers transitives. Add a test/CI step asserting a known-vulnerable transitive surfaces.

checks.question: Are container images built FROM untrusted base images with no provenance, or pulled at runtime by mutable tag (e.g. :latest) so the image can change between runs? (V15.2.2)

onYes.title: Fix V15.2.2: pin base images by digest; pull from trusted registries
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Mutable tags let images change under the runtime; untrusted bases ship vulnerabilities and possibly malware.

Find all instances: Inspect Dockerfiles and Helm/Kustomize manifests; identify tag-based pulls and questionable bases.

Fix correctly: Pin base images by digest (sha256:...). Use a curated internal registry. Scan images on build; gate on findings.

Acceptance: All image pulls are by digest from trusted sources. Add a CI policy check.

checks.question: Are cryptographic operations performed by hand-rolled implementations or by deprecated libraries instead of the platform's standard, audited primitives? (V11.4.1)

onYes.title: Fix V11.4.1: use platform-standard, audited cryptographic libraries
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Hand-rolled crypto has consistent issues (constant-time, key handling, padding). Deprecated libraries lack timely fixes.

Find all instances: Locate cryptographic operations; identify hand-rolled implementations and deprecated libraries.

Fix correctly: Replace with the platform's standard crypto library (libsodium/NaCl, BoringSSL, .NET's System.Security.Cryptography, Python's cryptography). Use high-level APIs (AEAD, password-hash) over primitives.

Acceptance: No hand-rolled crypto in security paths. Add a CI rule flagging direct-block-cipher use outside known wrappers.

checks.question: Do session cookies persist across browser sessions when they should be session-only (no max-age/expires), making compromised devices a permanent foothold? (V7.6.1)

onYes.title: Fix V7.6.1: scope session cookies to browser sessions where appropriate
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Persistent session cookies on shared/compromised devices outlive the user's browser session.

Find all instances: Inspect Set-Cookie for session cookies; check whether they carry Max-Age/Expires that exceed the intended scope.

Fix correctly: For session-only behaviour, omit Max-Age/Expires (or set Max-Age=0 on logout). Use server-side absolute timeout as the authoritative bound. Distinguish remember-me from session cookies.

Acceptance: Closing the browser ends the session. Add a test asserting Max-Age semantics.

checks.question: Is access to sensitive data not subject to fine-grained authorisation checks at the row/field level, so the API leaks data the caller is technically authorised to receive but should not see in bulk (mass-export abuse)? (V8.7.1)

onYes.title: Fix V8.7.1: bound bulk-data access by per-row authorisation and export limits
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Endpoints that return collections without row-level authorisation can be drained by abusive callers.

Find all instances: Locate list/search endpoints; check whether each row is checked against the caller's permissions and whether export caps apply.

Fix correctly: Enforce per-row authorisation (or query filters bound to the caller). Cap page size; require authentication and abuse signals for large queries; rate-limit bulk endpoints.

Acceptance: A low-privilege caller cannot mass-export. Add a test asserting limits and per-row checks.

checks.question: Does the application not validate file/path inputs against canonicalisation attacks (Unicode normalisation tricks, mixed slashes, encoded slashes)? (V5.2.2)

onYes.title: Fix V5.2.2: canonicalise file paths fully before authorisation/decisions
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Authorisation decisions made on non-canonical paths can be bypassed by Unicode tricks (\u002f, %2f, ..\\, NFKD-mapped slashes).

Find all instances: Locate code that authorises/uses file paths; check whether paths are normalised and re-validated post-canonicalisation.

Fix correctly: URL-decode once, normalise Unicode to NFC, resolve to absolute path, and confirm the result starts with the allowed root. Reject mixed slashes and encoded path separators.

Acceptance: Encoded-traversal payloads are refused. Add tests with %2f, NFKD-mapped variants, and Unicode look-alikes.

checks.question: Does the application not enforce subresource integrity (SRI) on third-party scripts and stylesheets it loads, leaving it exposed to CDN compromise? (V3.2.2)

onYes.title: Fix V3.2.2: pin external script/style integrity with SRI
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Third-party scripts loaded without SRI execute whatever the CDN serves, including compromised payloads.

Find all instances: Inspect HTML/SPA shells for <script src="//cdn..."> and <link rel="stylesheet" href="//cdn..."> tags without integrity attributes.

Fix correctly: Add integrity="sha384-..." and crossorigin="anonymous". Generate and update integrity hashes during build. Self-host critical scripts where feasible.

Acceptance: Every external script/style declares integrity. Add a CI step asserting SRI on all external <script>/<link> tags.

checks.question: Are integer arithmetic operations on untrusted values (sizes, counts, amounts) unchecked, allowing overflow/wrap/sign-flip to produce out-of-bounds states? (V2.1.2)

onYes.title: Fix V2.1.2: checked arithmetic and explicit bounds on untrusted integers
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Untrusted integers in arithmetic can overflow/wrap, leading to negative quantities, buffer-size underflow, or pricing bugs.

Find all instances: Locate arithmetic on user-derived integers in security-relevant code (sizes, indices, money).

Fix correctly: Use checked arithmetic (checked{} in C#, Math.addExact in Java, explicit overflow checks). Cap values at safe bounds before use. Use decimal types for money.

Acceptance: Overflow inputs produce explicit failures, not silent wraps. Add tests at boundary values.

checks.question: Does the codebase commit timing-side-channel-vulnerable comparisons (string equality of secrets/HMACs) instead of constant-time comparison? (V11.5.1)

onYes.title: Fix V11.5.1: use constant-time comparison for secrets
onYes.prompt:
Problem: == on secrets/HMACs leaks length and prefix information via timing, especially over networks.

Find all instances: Locate comparisons of HMACs, tokens, password hashes, MAC tags; check whether they use the platform's constant-time helper.

Fix correctly: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual, hmac.compare_digest, CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals, MessageDigest.isEqual. Wrap into a helper to make reuse easy.

Acceptance: All secret comparisons go through the constant-time helper. Add a test asserting equal-length but differing inputs return false.
